claim_boundary: Normal admitted-artifact selection now carries one full, revalidated resolved-action record across the Rust selector, HCLI resolver, terminal action, serve resident, HTTP switch, and Web reuse paths. The catalog owns the admission decision; Rust and transport boundaries validate and preserve its complete record. This does not unify raw research, AgentOS, or non-catalog model paths, and it does not establish byte-level verification of the legacy KIMI aggregate revision.
result_commit_ref: HEAD: the commit containing this receipt

canonical_owner.contract: hawking.resolved_action.v1 carries the action and execution intent; exact artifact id, canonical path, kind, revision, and revision basis; catalog identity and revision; grant identity, digest, admission, and supported actions; and a complete reuse binding. A transport must carry the full wire record and the receiving HCLI owner revalidates it against the current Gravity registry before use.

migrated_production_paths: crates/hawking/src/main.rs: hawking select <artifact> <action> asks the HCLI catalog for a typed action, structurally validates it, and forwards its original JSON only through --resolved-action-json
hcli/use.py: --resolve-only requires --action and emits the full record; ordinary use resolves serve before its HTTP switch
hcli/cli.py, hcli/app.py, and hcli/controller.py: the direct terminal accepts only an execute action, revalidates it, and does not reselect it through ModelRegistry
hcli/serve.py: typed startup, /v1/switch, direct-server construction, health, and completion all preserve and revalidate the admitted surface action
hcli/web.py: fresh startup and both explicit and implicit reuse forward the full Web action; equal paths do not bypass binding/action revalidation
deleted_or_replaced_policy: Rust's path-only ResolvedHcliArtifact selection result and production --model forwarding after a typed resolution
the Web same-path early-return that could retain an older serve binding instead of posting the requested Web action
serve completion's hard-coded resolve-as-serve behavior for a resident carrying another admitted surface action
necessary_adapters_retained: Rust invokes the Python catalog through a subprocess because the public selector and catalog live in different runtimes; it validates the record but does not recreate catalog policy.
JSON is the explicit process/HTTP transport at Rust-to-HCLI, HCLI-to-action, and Web-to-resident boundaries.

boundary_controls.python_resolution: The resolver emits only hawking.resolved_action.v1 with lower-case SHA-256-shaped revision fields, complete matching reuse binding, admitted grant, and a supported requested action.
boundary_controls.rust_resolution: The Rust resolver command is python -P -m hcli models <artifact> --resolve-only --action <action>. -P prevents the caller's working directory from shadowing the paired HCLI source root supplied through PYTHONPATH.
boundary_controls.transport: Rust preserves the resolver's original JSON serialization rather than rebuilding a smaller record from a path. The selected action process receives --resolved-action-json and no --model argument.
boundary_controls.serve_and_web: A typed serve action may be serve or web, never execute. A current request revalidates the resident's action before backend completion. Web reuse posts a full action even when the artifact path matches, so serve-to-web transitions cannot be silently skipped.
boundary_controls.failure_semantics: Malformed typed switch input returns HTTP 400; unavailable, revoked, stale, unsupported, or action-mismatched admission returns HTTP 403 before a backend request or replacement load.

evidence: workspace/campaign/odyssey/gravity-artifacts.json gives only prose saying SHA-256 covers ordered named files and bytes.
The value and prose entered in merge ac81444f177915a2f50888893f502408b52d0584; its history preserves no algorithm, delimiter/encoding, exact ordering rule, command, or aggregate preimage.
The bounded-freeze and bootstrap receipts retain individual file digests, but individual SHA-256 values cannot reconstruct a hash over raw concatenated file bytes.
hcli.catalog revalidates the current registry declaration and explicitly does not rehash a multi-shard artifact per action.
artifact_revision_integrity.meaning: The artifact revision is a legacy admitted-registry declaration. The historical aggregate preimage and serialization are not retained in this repository. This action was revalidated against the current registry binding, not rehashed against model bytes.
artifact_revision_integrity.reopen_condition: Define a versioned streaming pre-spawn algorithm and exact file manifest, then mint and verify a new revision. Do not guess an algorithm for b63fa8d4.

diff_ledger.interpretation: This is not a LOC-reduction claim. It deliberately adds a strict cross-process identity contract, revalidation checks, negative controls, and independent boundary tests while replacing weaker path-only production transports.

runtime_probe.purpose: Check resolver process overhead only; it does not run an action or initialize a backend.
runtime_probe.current_method: 31 sequential fresh subprocesses of python3 -P -m hcli models KIMI_P0_OPERATIONAL --resolve-only --action serve with the implementation source root on PYTHONPATH; each successful stdout value was parsed as JSON.

earlier_base_measurement.method: 31 sequential fresh legacy resolver subprocesses collected before the initial implementation commit

runtime_probe.interpretation: No gross resolver regression was observed. Cache state, ordering, and the new explicit action argument were uncontrolled, so these figures are not a causal speedup claim. Full selection still has one resolver process plus the selected action process.

remaining_duplicate_or_raw_authority: Generic HCLI still allows non-catalog local/native/GGUF/remote values through legacy ModelRegistry/RuntimePool selection. An admitted raw path is normalized to execute, but a non-catalog value remains outside this action contract.
AgentOS persists and exports a raw ResidentConfig.model/HCLI_MODEL_PATH model identity, then reconstructs its model independently.
Native qualification runners retain raw profile execution because they are a separate qualification surface.
Explicit research ModelLake switching retains raw research selection.
hcli.web.start_surface retains an internal raw --model fallback for legacy callers; the public Web route now supplies a typed action.
higher_order_removal_question: The contract now identifies the normal admitted route. The next practical deletion candidate is duplicated effective default/profile policy once its actual precedence is projected in one typed result; raw AgentOS and research paths require separate ownership decisions before they can be migrated or removed.
